sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Roermond is a small city with a very large outlet centre, and its parking policy is about keeping cars out of the old centre. The 2021 action plan for 2021 to 2030 targets street parking pressure inside the Singels of at most 90 percent at the peak, with street spaces kept for residents' first cars and short-stay visitors. Its staged measures start with Wilhelminaplein and garage-permit studies, then dearer second-car permits, no second permit for new residents, paid hours to 22:00 and finally a permit ceiling [6]. Its reason is the 2019 count, which found street pressure inside the Singels that could exceed 100 percent on weekday evenings and Saturdays, while the municipal garages mostly had room [7]. Paid hours for 2026 run Monday to Saturday from 08:00 to 22:00 and Sunday from 12:00 to 22:00 in areas A to D, and until 20:00 in area E, under a college decision of 19 August 2025 [3]. The 2026 street rate is 2.80 euros an hour in the Binnenstad, area A, 1.90 euros in areas B, C and D, and 1.70 euros in area E, with a double tariff after the second hour [0]. A first resident permit costs 12.00 euros a month, a second 33.00 and a visitor permit 0.24 euros an hour [2]. Scratch cards for visitors were to end from 1 January 2024 so that a scan vehicle can enforce, with 270 visitor hours a year in area A and 405 in areas B to E, according to a 2023 proposal [11].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: Several changes are proposals. A college proposal of December 2025 on the Wilhelminaplein final design assumes a generous halving of the square's parking capacity, with the remaining spaces mainly for residents, and suggests opening the Arlo car park round the clock during the works planned for the second half of 2026 [4]. Reconstruction of the Singelring phase 3 accepts about 20 percent fewer spaces; in its project area 16 of 90 spaces disappear and 11 are planned elsewhere, a net loss of 5 [5]. The action plan aims for 5 percent of spaces in the municipal garages to have a charge point by 2025 and 10 percent by 2030, from 4 of 400 at Kazerneplein and 3 of 350 at Stationspark when written, and names three park-and-bike candidates, all plans [8][16]. Minutes of 2019 show the station vision with a park-and-ride and bus boulevard at Veeladingstraat, with a question mark about the year [17]. The outlet's future vision asks for about 3,500 square metres more retail space and 1,500 more food and drink space, with an ambition of about 10 million visitors a year over time; the proposal says the extra traffic could not be handled on the existing infrastructure, and the vision itself is withheld [14].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality sets tariffs only in two garages, Kazerneplein (400 spaces) and Stationspark (541), which it operates with Q-Park as manager; Q-Park runs Oranjerie and Roercenter, and the outlet runs its own car parks P1, P2 and P3, according to a 2019 evaluation, so these arrangements and figures are old [9]. The 2026 municipal car-park rates are 1.90 euros an hour at Maashaven and Arlo, with a maximum of 11.00 euros, and 2.80 euros at Wilhelminaplein; Kazerneplein and Stationspark do not appear in the table [1]. Exit cards that traders resell to customers were priced equal to the outlet's day rate, and purchases rose from about 800 a month in 2019 to about 1,400 in early 2022 [10]. The outlet says the first 30 minutes in its car parks are free and a full day costs 7 euros, read on 21 October 2026 [12]. It draws over 8 million visitors a year, about 60 percent from Germany, and studies cited put the share also visiting the centre at 10 to 20 percent [13]. On 26 May 2022 many German day visitors jammed traffic, with delays of over an hour on the N280 [15].

Our data cover the two station park-and-rides for about 61 days since 22 August 2026. Veeladingstraat (151 spaces) averaged about 49% on weekdays and 42% at weekends and was nearly full on a Thursday morning, at its peak of 97%. Godsweerdersingel (100 spaces) averaged 26% on weekdays and 12% at weekends and reached 93% on a Tuesday morning. The garages in the centre and the outlet's car parks are not in our data.
